claim: Overview of Kuching must-try dishes: Sarawak laksa, kolo mee, ayam pansuh, midin, kek lapis.
quote: Sarawak Laksa features a signature creamy, spice-packed broth made from coconut milk, herbs, and prawns.

claim: Sarawak laksa best eaten early morning; midin is a Sarawak-only fern fried with garlic and belacan.
quote: Midin, a fern that grows only in Sarawak, these curly fern shoots are fried with garlic and either red wine or belacan.

claim: Tripadvisor ranking of best laksa restaurants in Kuching, updated 2026.
quote: THE BEST Laksa in Kuching (Updated March 2026) - Tripadvisor

claim: Local guide to Sarawak laksa spots including Chong Choon Cafe (Poh Lam), Mom's Laksa branches, Madam Tang's, opening before 10am.
quote: Poh Lam Laksa @ Chong Choon Cafe ... Opens early, typically sold out by 10AM; one size only; limited seating.

claim: Ah Mui Laksa moved to its own Madam Mui Laksa & Kopitiam on Jalan Rubber in Oct 2025; Mom's Laksa is Kuching's most famous brand.
quote: As of October 2025, Ah Mui Laksa moved from Foody Goody Cafe to its own coffeeshop called Madam Mui Laksa and Kopitiam on Jalan Rubber.

claim: Choon Hui Cafe on Ban Hock Road opens 7.30am, sells out before lunch, famous Sarawak laksa.
quote: Choon Hui Cafe opens at 7.30am. There are lots of people in the morning and things usually finish before lunch.

claim: Anthony Bourdain ate Sarawak laksa at Choon Hui Cafe in 2005 (No Reservations) and 2015 (Parts Unknown).
quote: Bourdain visited twice in 2005 for Travel Channel's No Reservation and in 2015 for CNN's Parts Unknown.

claim: Anthony Bourdain returned to Kuching to eat Sarawak laksa in 2015.
quote: It's Sarawak laksa again for Bourdain

claim: Best kolo mee spots in Kuching; dry tossed egg noodles with char siu, minced pork and shallot oil.
quote: Kolo mee is a dry tossed noodle dish featuring springy egg noodles mixed with aromatic oils, accompanied by char siu or minced pork.

claim: Top Spot Food Court is an open-air rooftop seafood court atop a multi-storey car park.
quote: Topspot Food Court ... a slightly odd open-air eatery located on top of a multi-storey car park.

claim: Top Spot stall No.25 Bukit Mata Seafood lets diners pick fresh seafood from tanks; midin, prawns, crab cooked to order.
quote: Stall No. 25 Bukit Mata Seafood is known for their affordable rates and fresh seafood. You can choose your catch directly from tanks.

claim: Kuching street food spots: Top Spot, Open Air Market, Satok Weekend Market, India Street, Carpenter Street.
quote: Open Air Market (City Centre) - Historic breakfast destination with Sarawak Laksa stalls and Kolo Mee vendors.

claim: Black Bean Coffee old-school cafe (20+ years, gula apong latte, 1-hour limit); Lau Ya Keng kueh chap; Choon Hui laksa.
quote: Black Bean Coffee ... Quirky, old-school coffee shop operating for over 20 years ... Iced Gula Apong Latte (top-seller) ... One-hour sitting limit maintained.

claim: Umai is a Melanau speciality of raw fish cured in calamansi/lime; midin stir-fried with garlic and belacan.
quote: A Melanau speciality, Umai is thinly sliced raw fish cured in calamansi juice, with onions, chillies, and ginger.

claim: Locals recommend Lepau Restaurant and KANTIN at The Granary for midin; Top Spot and Sin Soon Lee also good.
quote: Lepau Restaurant in Kuching and the KANTIN at The Granary Kuching are recommended by locals for trying Midin.

claim: The Dyak serves native Kenyah cuisine (pansuh, kasam, terong asam); guide to indigenous food in Kuching.
quote: The Dyak serves native Kenyah cuisine from Pansuh to Kasam (fermented poultry/fish) and terong asam.

claim: The Dyak is decorated with Dayak motifs and is the place for fine dining indigenous food.
quote: The Dyak is tastefully decorated with Dayak motifs and is the place to go if you are looking for fine dining.

claim: Ayam pansuh / manuk pansuh is chicken cooked in bamboo with tapioca leaves, central to Gawai Dayak festival.
quote: The Ibans and the Bidayuhs from western Borneo traditionally prepare this dish during festivals, especially during the Gawai Dayak.

claim: Manok pansoh marinated with lemongrass, ginger, galangal, torch ginger; served with sambal belacan.
quote: the chicken is mixed and marinated with aromatic ingredients, including onions, ginger, lemongrass, garlic, torch ginger flower, and galangal.

claim: Pinggai Cafe on China Street, run by Iban sisters since Aug 2018, serves modern Dayak dishes and tuak cocktails.
quote: Our signature dishes are influenced by traditional Dayak flavour, which comes from Iban and Bidayuh culinary style of cooking.

claim: The Dyak is at Simpang Tiga (~2km SE of Chinatown), open Mon-Sat 11am-9pm, celebrates Dayak cuisine.
quote: The Dyak is a charming restaurant located 2km southeast of Old Chinatown ... It opens from Monday to Saturday, from 11 am to 9 pm.

claim: Lepau on Jalan Ban Hock; tribal-fusion Sarawak cuisine (Iban, Bidayuh, Kelabit, Kayan, Melanau), featured in National Geographic.
quote: Lepau is Kuching's most recognized establishment for Sarawak cuisine, operating for over a decade with features in National Geographic.

claim: Kek Lapis Warisan has an open kitchen to watch baking and offers samples; premium flavours.
quote: an open kitchen where visitors can watch the baking process ... samples available to try before buying.

claim: Maria Kek Lapis sits by the waterfront with many samples and a wide colourful selection.
quote: Located by the waterfront with plenty of samples to try and lots of cake choices.

claim: Kek Lapis Mama Su on Jalan Main Bazaar offers 40+ flavours of layer cake.
quote: Mama Su offers freshly baked and colorful layer cakes ... over 40 flavors in total, including kek kukus, kek bakar and kek roll.

claim: Mira Cake House is a Kuching kek lapis Sarawak / kek lapis basah maker.
quote: Mira Cake House | Kek Lapis Sarawak | Kek Lapis Basah | Kuching, Sarawak, Malaysia

claim: Abg K'ju Cake House sells a 10-layer Luxury Kek Lapis Sultan at RM1,800 per tray; 500+ loaves sold in early 2026.
quote: Abg K'ju Cake House offers a ten-layer 'Luxury Kek Lapis Sultan' priced at RM1,800 per tray ... sold over 500 loaves.

claim: RG Ais Krim pioneered gula apong-topped soft-serve in Kuching from 2006; based at Tower/Open Air Market with Satok and i-Com outlets.
quote: RG Ais Krim operates at the Tower Market (Open Air Market) on Jalan Gertak ... In 2006, Richard innovated by introducing a gula apong topping.

claim: Gula apong is palm sugar from the nipah palm, native to Sarawak's swamps.
quote: Gula Apong is a type of palm sugar extracted from the nipah palm tree, native to the swamps of Sarawak.

claim: Guide to must-try cendol and ais kacang (ABC) stalls in Kuching including Swee Kang.
quote: 10 MUST TRY Cendol & ABC stalls in Kuching

claim: Swee Kang Ais Kacang is praised for cendol with smooth gula apong.
quote: the smooth taste of their gula apong + cendol.

claim: Bumbu Cooking Class at 57 Carpenter Street: market tour, 3 dishes, recipe book; host Joseph.
quote: Bumbu Cooking is located at No 57 Carpenter Street ... The classes include 3 dishes, market tour, and recipe book.

claim: Bumbu Cooking Class official site, Carpenter Street, Kuching.
quote: Bumbu Cooking Class - Home

claim: Paradesa 6-hour Kuching walking tour + cooking class: Petanak Market, sampan crossing, Dayak menu, MYR 310.
quote: Participants visit Petanak Market ... then take a traditional sampan boat to reach the market from the Waterfront.

claim: Satok Weekend Market is a major Kuching market attraction with food and produce.
quote: Satok Weekend Market (2026) - All You MUST Know Before You Go

claim: Satok (Medan Niaga Satok) is on the north bank of the Sarawak River, busiest Sat evening/Sun morning, opens from 5am, sells wild ferns and exotic fruit.
quote: The Sunday market starts business as early as 5am in the morning ... unique wild ferns and exotic vegetables that are almost impossible to find in West Malaysia.

claim: Open Air Market (Tower Market) on Jalan Power is a heritage hawker food court.
quote: Kuching Open Air Market (Tower Market)

claim: Open Air Market stalls serve tomato char kueh tiaw, beef noodle, and seafood from afternoon to late night.
quote: Try the tomato Char Kueh Tiaw. The tomato sauce is delectable.

claim: Carpenter Street is Kuching's oldest street; Lau Ya Keng hawker centre by the temple is known for kueh chap and kolo mee.
quote: The hawkers centre in front of the temple (Lay Ya Geng) was always renowned for various foods ... well known for the Kueh Chap.

claim: India Street (Lebuh India) in Old Kuching has Indian-Muslim and Sarawakian eateries and stalls.
quote: a fantastic place to indulge in the local culinary scene, with numerous smaller eateries and stalls.

claim: Royal Kuching Cruise offers Sarawak Heritage and other menus with live sape music on the Sarawak River.
quote: a selection of menus ranging from Sarawak Heritage Cuisine to Western Cuisine to English Hi-tea.

claim: Sarawak River Cruise sells lunch/dinner dining packages on the river.

claim: Hilton Kuching riverside dining serves Pansoh Manuk (bamboo chicken) with tuak rice wine.
quote: sample local dishes such as Pansoh Manuk (bamboo chicken with fragrant rice) accompanied by local tuak rice wine.

claim: Annah Rais Bidayuh longhouse day trip (~60km, 90min) with bamboo chicken, wild ferns and tuak rice wine on the tanju.
quote: delight in freshly cooked bamboo chicken and wild ferns as you unwind on the tanju, the longhouse's welcoming verandah.

claim: Kuching day tour to Annah Rais longhouse includes an ethnic Bidayuh lunch.
